declared.title: Outcome versus process focused future thinking: results from a randomised experiment
declared.foundIn: reports/choose-your-struggle/counter-evidence.md (cards 2 and 6); Crossref search « Hallford outcome-focused process-focused thinking anticipatory pleasure motivation preregistered » (2026-11-26)

population: 134 adults online (mean age 35) who imagined personally relevant future events, randomly told to focus on outcomes or on steps

findings.text: Thinking about the outcome of a future event raised anticipatory pleasure, motivation and personal significance

support.sentence: Outcome-focused thinking increased anticipatory pleasure, motivation and personal significance.

findings.text: Thinking about the steps lowered perceived control and went with less anticipated and anticipatory pleasure

support.sentence: In contrast, process-focused thinking reduced perceived control and was associated with reductions in both anticipated and anticipatory pleasure.

limits: self-reported feelings right after the task: no effort, behaviour or result measured
imagined events, not a goal pursued afterwards; preregistered, one online sample
country not given in the abstract; no sample from the Middle East or North Africa known
